rationale: The conversion target is the existing upstream qcom,lpass-va-macro driver and its existing DT binding schema. The upstream schema already documents the accepted SoC-specific compatible strings, clock inputs, power domains, qcom,dmic-sample-rate, vdd-micb-supply, and clock-output-names/fsgen output. The remaining downstream-only DT interfaces found in the transformed downstream source are not valid upstream binding deltas and should not be documented as new ABI. Therefore Patch-07 is skipped rather than adding a binding patch that would preserve downstream-private interfaces.
series_note: Patch-07 is skipped. The final conversion series is six patches. If the patch subjects are regenerated for mailing, use [PATCH 0/6] through [PATCH 6/6] rather than retaining the earlier reviewer-model [PATCH n/7] numbering.

upstream_binding.fsgen_handling: fsgen is documented as clock-output-names in the upstream binding, matching upstream driver behavior. No new fsgen input clock binding is required.

post_six_patch_generated_source_check.reason: These names are downstream-private compatibility interfaces. A binding patch that adds them would expand upstream ABI rather than align to the existing upstream VA macro architecture.

krzysztof_kozlowski.likely_objection: Do not add undocumented downstream-private compatible strings or properties without real upstream users and schema justification.
krzysztof_kozlowski.decision_impact: Skipping Patch-07 avoids creating unnecessary DT ABI.

mark_brown.likely_objection: ASoC driver conversion should use existing upstream bindings unless hardware support genuinely requires a DT ABI extension.
mark_brown.decision_impact: No binding delta keeps the driver conversion focused on source cleanup and upstream framework alignment.

srinivas_kandagatla.likely_objection: Qualcomm LPASS macro bindings already cover the upstream VA macro resource model.
srinivas_kandagatla.decision_impact: Existing qcom,lpass-va-macro.yaml remains the binding authority.
